about.title: Windsor Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Windsor residents rely on a small circle of local clinics and specialists, plus larger Sonoma County hospital systems for more complex care. When a diagnosis is missed, a surgery goes wrong, or medication is mismanaged, the harm can follow a patient for years. California treats these claims differently than a typical injury case — MICRA sets tighter notice rules, a shorter window to act, and requires input from a qualified medical expert before a case can move forward. That doesn't mean every bad outcome qualifies, and it doesn't mean you're without options. If you or a family member were hurt by substandard care in Windsor, LawProactive can connect you, free of charge, with an independent attorney who reviews malpractice matters and can tell you honestly whether your situation warrants a closer look. There's no obligation, and attorneys in this network only get paid if your case recovers money.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before the Clock Runs Out

items.title: MICRA's Strict Deadlines
items.desc: California generally gives you one year from when you discover the harm, and never more than three years from the injury itself, to bring a claim. Missing either window can end a case regardless of its merits.

items.title: 90-Day Notice Requirement
items.desc: Before filing suit, California law requires sending the healthcare provider a 90-day notice of intent. An attorney familiar with this step can help make sure it's done correctly and on time.

items.title: Expert Review Is Almost Always Needed
items.desc: Because a poor outcome alone doesn't prove malpractice, a qualified medical expert typically must confirm that care fell below an accepted standard. Attorneys in this network work with those experts to evaluate whether a claim holds up.

items.question: I had a bad outcome after treatment in Windsor — does that mean malpractice happened?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California law is clear that an unfavorable result by itself isn't proof of malpractice; the care given has to have fallen below what a reasonably careful provider would have done. An attorney can help you understand whether your specific facts suggest a departure from that standard.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a claim after discovering the harm?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you one year from when you discover, or reasonably should have discovered, the injury, and no more than three years from the date of the injury itself. There are limited exceptions, so it's worth getting a timeline reviewed sooner rather than later.

items.question: Do I need to go to a hospital outside Windsor for my case to matter?
items.answer: No — whether the care happened at a local Windsor clinic or a larger Sonoma County facility, the same California rules apply. LawProactive connects Windsor residents with independent attorneys who evaluate cases regardless of exactly where treatment occurred.
